= Cache

The cache configuration defines the datastores where tiles should be stored/retrieved. We recommended you use a `multi`-tiered cache with a smaller, faster "near" cache first followed by a larger, slower "far" cache.

Some cache options include their own built-in mechanisms for applying a TTL and maximum size, and some don't. On top of that, xref:configuration/layer.adoc[layers] support a `cachettl` option that's honored uniformly no matter which cache is configured: for a cache backend with no native concept of expiry, tilegroxy emulates it by recording when an entry was written and treating it as a miss once `cachettl` has passed, which causes the tile to be regenerated and the stale entry overwritten on the next request. This doesn't replace a backend's own TTL or size limits, it's a floor that works everywhere.

There is still no way to explicitly invalidate a layer, or a bounding box/zoom range within it, on demand (for example after upstream data changes) short of purging the backing store by hand. A cache that manages its own maximum size otherwise requires an external cleanup mechanism if desired. Be mindful of this as some options may incur their own costs if allowed to grow unchecked.

When specifying a cache ensure you include the `name` parameter.
